A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoWorld and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original H2O benchmark results, conditioning and backbone ablations, and qualitative TACO, real-world, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative evaluations on additional datasets, pose-modeling comparisons, robustness tests, component analyses, and a video extension.

M1.justification: The principal two-stage pipeline, architecture, and losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.2.7 adds an implemented video-generation adaptation: subsequent frames combine the previous generated latent with fresh noise at a 1:9 ratio. v1 only proposed temporal integration as future work.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained H2O, TACO, and smartphone examples, v2 actually evaluates Assembly101 and Ego-Exo4D, which v1 only cited. It also introduces a selected occluded/blurry H2O test scenario and evaluates sequential video generation.

E2.justification: The H2O comparator set is retained, but TACO expands from qualitative comparison with CFLD to quantitative comparisons also including pix2pixHD and pixelNeRF. Tables B-C add body-pose, camera-pose, and CNN-based hand-pose alternatives. The claimed 4Diff comparison reinterprets an existing no-pose/no-text ablation; it is not a separately implemented 4Diff baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds PA-MPJPE using HaMeR and CLIPScore to the original four image metrics. New protocols include pose-estimation MPJPE, manually selected noisy cases, predicted-versus-ground-truth component controls, and temporal evaluation using T-LPIPS and Flow-warp. The documented core training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables B-H add analyses of pose-modeling strategies, MANO versus keypoints, noisy inputs, component accuracy and removal, and temporal consistency versus image quality. The incorrect-text study is revised with new examples involving appearance attributes. Existing backbone and generation-consistency analyses are retained, while the TACO failure examples are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions show four generations per input in the qualitative consistency analysis. Neither reports quantitative uncertainty estimates, training-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures; v2's additional tables retain point estimates.

E6.justification: The original four-metric H2O, conditioning, and backbone scores are retained. v2 adds metrics and substantial new results, including EgoWorld FIDs of 37.191, 50.232, and 61.231 on TACO, Assembly101, and Ego-Exo4D. Table H reports improved temporal consistency but worse FID with video extension, 35.455 versus 33.284. Several real-world outputs are also replaced; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1-7 are substantively unchanged; changing the depth-stabilization symbol is not a mathematical revision. No new theorem, proof, or theoretical derivation appears. The added temporal measures concern empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly extend the state-of-the-art claim from H2O and TACO to Assembly101 and Ego-Exo4D. The central contributions—single-image translation using geometric and semantic observations, diffusion reconstruction, and generalization to unseen scenarios—remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking hand visibility and global context to pose-modeling performance, and multimodal conditioning to the limited benefit of MANO representations. Its revised incorrect-text discussion emphasizes semantic control with preserved geometry, whereas v1 emphasized incorrect objects and VLM dependence. It also interprets estimated-input robustness and the temporal-consistency/image-quality tradeoff, while dropping the specific TACO head-visibility restriction.

D1.justification: v2 adds approximate reconstruction and pose-training times of 10 and 20 hours and specifies the video mixing ratio. Most architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and project-access information is retained. However, it removes v1's explicit H2O/TACO ground-truth-input provisions, H2O-only pose-estimator training restriction, and identification of the checkpoint used for real-world examples.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion is largely retained. v2 adds references for HaMeR, CLIPScore, ResNet, Hand4Whole, OSX, Gemini, and AnimateDiff. It newly positions CFLD as an upper-bound reference for Exo2Ego and the existing unconditioned ablation as a proxy for 4Diff.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the results narrative and reorganizes the paper: reconstruction implementation and backbone analysis move to the appendix, incorrect-text analysis moves into the main text, and limitations are consolidated. The appendix gains a broader subsection structure and an LLM-usage statement. Citation style and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and appendix Tables B-H, expands retained tables with metric columns, and substantially recomposes Figure 4. The incorrect-text figure gains sparse-map panels and changes examples; other figures are relocated or shortened, and the TACO failure figure disappears. Conference formatting also changes typography and page composition.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central claims through two additional datasets, hand-pose and semantic metrics, and component analyses. Particularly valuable is Table F's quantitative evaluation with fully predicted inputs, addressing a gap left by v1's ground-truth-assisted benchmarks and qualitative full-pipeline examples. The revision loses some explicit setup disclosures and TACO failure evidence, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. Nevertheless, the new evidence substantially improves assessment of generalization, component dependence, and practical tradeoffs.
